newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish c.bank dollar buying send zloty tumbling.
newsitem.headline: Polish c.bank dollar buying send zloty tumbling.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland bought an estimated $30 million through interventions on Wednesday, pulling the rug out from under the zloty and re-establishing three percent from parity as resistance.
"Today's intervention means the central bank wants three percent from the parity rate to be the barrier," said Przemyslaw Ciszecki, senior forex dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.
Dealers said the NBP first intervened after the zloty strengthened to 3.6 percent from the parity rate and knocked it down more than half a percentage point by close.
"The central bank suggested that 3.5 percent from parity is too strong and that three percent is where the zloty should be," said Magloszata Sawicka from Bank Handlowy SA.
The zloty closed at 2.98/2.75 percent from the trading band centre, down from Tuesday's 3.58/3.50 percent close.
It closed at 3.0500/60 to the dollar, down from 3.0360/80 on Tueday and at 1.8035/80 to the mark, down from 1.7845/65.

The central bank bought currencies at serveral levels today, with the latest round of interventions at 3.0531 zlotys per dollar and 1.8040 zlotys per mark, which is about 2.91 percent from the trading band centre.

Several dealers said that before the NBP started buying currencies on Wednesday some foreign investors began to sell small amounts of Polish treasuries to take advantage of the relatively strong zloty exchange rate.

But dealers said the zloty may be under further upward pressure in the near-term as foreign investors were expected to bid for larger amounts of Polish 12-percent five-year fixed bonds at Thursday's 200 million zloty primary auction.
"The central bank's interventions, which knocked the zloty down, were a present for foreign investors who are hungry for Polish fixed bonds," said one dealer at a major London bank.
On the money market one-day rates eased as banks found excess cash after squaring reserve positions, dealers said.
Overnight rates fell to 20.75/21.20 percent from opening's 21.10/21.45 percent and tomorrow/next rates to 21.80/21.15 percent from Tuesday's close 21.25/21.65.
Some dealers said that money market liquidity increased because banks started selling bonds from their portfolios in anticipation of yield increases at future auctions.
